description:
The output layer exposes macros, constructors and helpers that nothing calls. The exit-code descriptions are hand-copied into the schema generator.

## Background

These items have no caller in any crate:

- The `output_message!` and `output_json!` macros (`crates/jit/src/output_macros.rs:6,47`).
- `JsonError::invalid_state`, `invalid_priority` and `gate_validation_failed` (`output.rs:1211,1217,1226`).
- `ExitCode::all_codes_documentation` (`output.rs:622`).
- `OutputContext::print_error`, `is_quiet` and `is_json` (`output.rs:366,371,376`).

`JsonError::from_code_text` (`output.rs:490`) has only test callers (`output.rs:3361,3647`). `ExitCode::description` (`output.rs:600`) is called only by `all_codes_documentation`, while `schema.rs:835-881` `generate_exit_codes()` hand-copies the same ten descriptions string for string.

Six `allow(dead_code)` attributes (`output.rs:463,469,528,553,592,1179`) suppress nothing: `output` is a public module (`lib.rs:24`), so `dead_code` never fires on its public items. `ErrorCode::ALL` shows the enumeration pattern.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The listed macros, `JsonError` constructors, `ExitCode::all_codes_documentation`, the three `OutputContext` methods and `JsonError::from_code_text` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: `generate_exit_codes` takes each description from `ExitCode::description` over an exit-code enumeration, and the generated exit-code reference is byte-identical.
- [hard] REQ-03: `output.rs` holds no `allow(dead_code)`.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every remaining output macro, `JsonError` constructor, `ExitCode` helper and `OutputContext` method has a production caller.

## Notes

If `output_macros.rs` ends up empty, the file and its module declaration go with it.
title: Prune the uncalled output surface
